resources.string: Blocked apps have no Internet access.
Blocked apps have Internet access. Tap to open.
Android did not allow the firewall to start.
No blocked attempts yet. Only apps you block appear here.
Stored in memory only and erased when the firewall restarts.

AppWall cuts Internet access for the apps you choose. It has no Internet permission and no ads or analytics.

Only blocked apps go through its local VPN, where their traffic is dropped. All other apps bypass it, so AppWall never sees their traffic.

It lists connection attempts from blocked apps. It cannot show where allowed apps connect.

If AppWall stops, blocked apps get their Internet access back. It restarts after a phone restart or an update, but blocked apps have Internet access from power-on until after your first unlock, plus the time AppWall takes to start. Blocking or unblocking an app also leaves a very short gap while Android rebuilds the VPN.

Only one VPN can run per profile, so starting another VPN turns AppWall off. Each work profile needs its own copy of AppWall.

A blocked app can still get data through other apps or system services, such as a browser it opens, a download service or push notifications.

Do not turn on "Block connections without VPN" for AppWall: it would cut the network for every app.
